I have the source material and the voice rules. Here is the draft.

**Subject:** ASEI AI in Action workshop: what we decided and what I need built

Hi Alice,

We had the ASEI prep call yesterday and I want to get you the substance while it's fresh, because you're building the segment from it.

The event is the evening of November 17 at our office. Networking and food from 5 to 6, ASEI kicks it off for about ten minutes, Ric does a ten minute welcome on Improving, and I have 6:20 to 8:00. Target is 50 to 60 people in the room, and realistically the room stops being comfortable past 70, so build for a room, not an auditorium. Bethany is running logistics and is packaging the promotion assets, which means Neha's flyer, Ric's bio and headshot, and whatever material I'm using. Neha is also updating the flyer, which currently lists Curtis instead of Ric.

The audience is corporate, mid-level managers and leaders, not students. Becky Caleb, who runs consumer vehicle lending technology at Bank of America and is one of the ASEI leads on this, was very specific about the outcome she wants. Something practical people can act on Monday, not a survey of AI. She called out Copilot pointers for personal productivity as one thing her people keep asking for, and a view of how leaders are organizing work now. Her framing stuck with me: every company is pushing AI training at people and nobody knows what to take in and what to ignore, so the filtering guidance is half the value.

That's why the eight stage maturity model is the spine of the session. Stage one is not really using AI, stage eight is agentic workflows doing the actual work, and the middle moves from AI as a tool I use, to AI as an assistant doing the work, to workflows that run themselves. It's a common vocabulary, not a scorecard. What I need built is the practical layer on top: at stage two, here's what you're doing differently on Monday, and here's the gate that gets you to stage three, and so on. Becky asked for a visual of the model specifically, and she wants to see it early enough to give input before we lock it, so that diagram is the first thing to get right.

The other design constraint is altitude. Becky wants it generic enough that a director and a senior manager each walk out with something, and concrete enough that nobody feels either talked down to or lost. She used a gym membership analogy, everybody signs up for the level they can actually handle, and I think that's exactly the right frame. Plan for mixed altitude rather than one track.

I also want a one page takeaway people carry out of the room. That matters as much as the content, because Becky's test is whether someone leaves with something they can do this week. One wrinkle on format: ASEI wants to simulcast to other chapters over Teams or Zoom, which could take it from 60 in the room to a couple hundred virtual, and if the format lands here they want to roll it to other chapters, so this first one is a template rather than a one time event. The virtual audience is listening rather than interacting, so all the interaction design stays in the room, but it does mean we can't lean on long silent exercises.

So here's what I need from you. Build the maturity model visual first so Becky can react to it this week, then the per stage practical guidance, the Copilot and productivity material, the leader's view of organizing work, and the one page takeaway. This week is the promotion window and Bethany needs the material to circulate, so a Becky ready draft this week is the real deadline. Please also pull my headshot and current bio so Bethany can hand them to Neha for the flyer.

Let me know what you need from me to get moving.


Thanks,

**Notes for David before this goes anywhere**

Date discrepancy worth a look: Bethany corrected the date on the call to the seventeenth ("I do have on the calendar the seventeenth of November in the evening, not the eighteenth"), and nobody pushed back, but Neha had said the eighteenth earlier. The draft uses the seventeenth. Confirm before send.

Also flagging: the flyer currently lists Curtis rather than Ric, which is why Neha is updating it. Included in the draft as context for the headshot and bio handoff, drop it if you'd rather handle that separately.

Nothing was sent, and no Outlook draft was created. This is text only, per your instruction.
